title: Renewal & expansion check-in — Argent Financial
summary: Check-in to discuss upcoming renewal, request for additional reserved capacity, and onboarding of EU region. Agreed to review pricing for 2-year committed term with added nodes in EU, run performance benchmark, and share SOC2/KMS docs. Action items assigned to both Redwood and Argent stakeholders.
topics: Adding EU region and data residency
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hi everyone, thanks for joining — Maya from Redwood here. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Laura Kim: Laura here, hi.
[00:08] Rajiv Singh: Rajiv, SRE.
[00:10] Nina Torres: Nina from procurement.
[00:12] Diego Alvarez: Diego, SE on the Redwood side.
[00:15] Maya Patel: Great, appreciate it. We're on for about 45 minutes — main goal is renewal & expansion check-in, specifically capacity and EU region request.
[00:28] Laura Kim: Yep, so our contract is up in six weeks, and traffic has been higher than projections. We're looking at adding reserved capacity, and also need EU region for data residency.
[00:36] Maya Patel: Okay understood. Diego, quick overview on options?
[00:40] Diego Alvarez: Sure. So we have Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. For what you're describing — steady high throughput plus EU residency — Dedicated in EU or Redwood Private in your VPC are the usual patterns. Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput; Private gives you more control over networking and KMS. There's also hybrid routing so you can keep most traffic on Hosted and burst to Dedicated.
[01:05] Rajiv Singh: Latency is key for us; front-end SLAs are 200ms for critical flows. Are we confident Dedicated in eu-west1 can hit that?
[01:12] Diego Alvarez: For short sequences yes — we've seen 60—120ms p99 on nn-optimized models. Depends on model variant and quantization. Also KV cache and continuous batching can reduce effective latency if you're repeating prompts.
[01:26] Laura Kim: We're using a small context right now, mostly 128 tokens average, high QPS. Currently on Hosted in us-central.
[01:33] Maya Patel: Makes sense. On pricing, we can present a 1-year vs 2-year committed option. 2-year gives better unit pricing and capacity priority.
[01:42] Nina Torres: Procurement will need details — what's included in dedicated? SLA levels? Audit stuff?
[01:47] Diego Alvarez: Dedicated includes reserved GPUs, autoscale policy controls (min/max pool sizes), monthly committed throughput, and access to logs and tracing. SLAs are tiered — you can opt into a higher SLA for an add-on.
[01:57] Nina Torres: We'll need SOC 2 and encryption details, KMS/HSM support.
[02:02] Diego Alvarez: We have SOC 2 Type II; I can share the pack. KMS integrations supported for Redwood Private; for Dedicated we offer customer-managed KMS via integrations with major cloud KMS. HSM is enterprise add-on.
[02:15] Laura Kim: Good. One question on data egress — if we add EU region, will requests from EU stay in-region?
[02:20] Maya Patel: Yes you can pin routes by region. We can route all EU customer traffic to EU nodes. For Private, traffic never leaves your VPC unless you configure cross-region.
[02:28] Rajiv Singh: For benchmarking, Diego, can you run the same load profile we're planning — 5k rps burst with sustained 800 rps?
[02:35] Diego Alvarez: We can run a perf job against a staging model; I just need your traffic shape and sample prompts. We'll simulate the KV cache hit patterns too.
[02:44] Laura Kim: I'll send the telemetry and a sample prompt set.
[02:47] Maya Patel: Great. Pricing discussion — hypothetically if you do a 2-year commit for Dedicated EU + US with 30% more capacity, you save about 18% on unit token cost vs month-to-month hosted. We can put exact numbers in a refreshed quote.
[03:03] Nina Torres: We need line items in the quote for committed capacity, burstable capacity, and region fee. Also any support SLA charges.
[03:10] Maya Patel: Absolutely. We'll include three options: 1-year renewal with moderate capacity bump, 2-year committed with deeper discounts and reserved EU nodes, and a Private pilot for regulated flows.
[03:20] Rajiv Singh: Quick technical — what about model fallbacks? If Dedicated capacity hits a limit, do we failover to hosted?
[03:25] Diego Alvarez: Yes, smart routing can fail over to a compatible hosted model or a lower-cost variant. You can set policy to prefer latency over cost or vice versa. There is a brief cold-start penalty if we spin new containers, but reserved pools avoid that.
[03:38] Laura Kim: Any estimation of warmup time for KV cache on rolling deploys?
[03:42] Diego Alvarez: Typically warmup is proportional to unique prefix volume; with continuous caching and pre-warm scripts we can get most hot prefixes populated in minutes. For large corpora it can be longer. We'll document the recommended pre-warm steps.
[03:55] Nina Torres: For procurement, timeline: we aim to sign by Oct 15th if pricing looks right.
[03:59] Maya Patel: That's feasible. Next steps we'll send an updated quote by Sep 18, perf benchmark scheduled week of Sep 28, and provide SOC2/KMS docs in the next two days.
[04:10] Rajiv Singh: Also can we get an SLA matrix — p50/p90/p99 numbers and allowable downtime?
[04:15] Diego Alvarez: I'll pull the SLA matrix and include it.
[04:18] Laura Kim: One more — can you confirm data retention defaults and options to shorten retention for EU?
[04:22] Maya Patel: Yes, retention configurable per-tenant; we'll include options and costs.
[04:27] Nina Torres: We'll need contract language around data residency and audit access.
[04:30] Maya Patel: Noted. Diego, anything else on the infra side?
[04:33] Diego Alvarez: For the perf test I suggest we test both the quantized 4-bit variant and the FP16 for comparison; one is cheaper but might add latency. Also we'll capture token cost metrics.
[04:45] Rajiv Singh: Good — that's important.
[04:47] Laura Kim: Ok, wrapping up — to recap: Redwood to send quote (1yr/2yr/private), Diego to run perf tests, Redwood to share SOC2/KMS docs and SLA matrix; Argent to share traffic patterns and procurement timeline.
[04:58] Maya Patel: Thanks all. We'll follow up with notes and the quote.
[05:02] Nina Torres: Thanks.
[05:05] (call ends)

Note: transcription contains occasional mis-hears — e.g., "Redwood De-dedicated" instead of Dedicated, "KV cache" sometimes transcribed as "K V cash" in auto transcript.
